title: Back in Wilkes-Barre: his father and bandleader Guy Hall
summary: After graduating he was undecided; his father was street superintendent, and Guy Hall, composer of Johnson Rag, led a local band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You're back home in Wilkes Barre?
I'm back in Wilkes Barre and I figured that --
What did your family -- what did your father do?
Well, my father was interested in politics, local politics. He had a political job, superintendent of the streets of -- well, how would you call it? Superintendent of the streets was his title.
Improving the roads and keeping the roads --

That's correct. That sort of thing. The road was a road department, and they could have sent me away to school as far as that's concerned, but it was a kick to be able to pay my way. I didn't have to write home for money or anything like that. So now that I'm out, I really didn't know what to do. There was a guy that I had been playing with there, a fellow by the name of Guy Hall. He had an orchestra around there for years, and he wrote the "Johnson Rag," incidentally.

But in those days -- we played it, but in those days it was a different Johnson Rag then when Glenn Miller and Jimmy and Russ Morgan did, made records of it. They added a little bit in there to make it commercial and to -- I think they had some lyrics written to it.

Anyway, I didn't want to play with them. I didn't want to go away to school and come back and play with them, an orchestra I had been playing with. If I couldn't do it myself, why, and I didn't know where to look. I found out later I could have looked a lot of places. I was a stick in the mud guy I guess.
